transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/time: 2026-06-29 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~60 minutes
- Attendees: Ava Mitchell (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Dr. Lena Park (NovaHealth Head of AI), Markus Lee (Director Eng), Priya Shah (Security)

Summary: quick kickoff, align on success metrics for clinical summarization POC, define eval artifacts and timeline.

[00:00] Ava Mitchell: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, really appreciate you taking the time. quick round of intros?
[00:10] Dr. Lena Park: Lena Park, Head of AI at NovaHealth, hi all.
[00:14] Markus Lee: Markus, Director of Engineering, I'll own infra questions.
[00:18] Priya Shah: Priya, security and compliance.
[00:20] Diego Ramos: Diego from Redwood, engineering, hi.
[00:22] Ava Mitchell: Awesome. so objective today is to scope the POC, align on success criteria, workload sizing, and most importantly the quality evaluation plan — golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination and format checks, and how we'll score results.

[00:40] Dr. Lena Park: Great. our primary use case is clinical note summarization and a small NER extraction for meds/conditions. priority is accuracy and minimal hallucination because this feeds downstream clinical workflows. latency is secondary but we do care about throughput, around 100 concurrent requests during peaks.

[01:05] Diego Ramos: Got it. for the POC we typically run a two-track evaluation: functional quality (accuracy, hallucination, format adherence) and performance (latency, cost). we recommend a 4-week POC with week 1 onboarding and data prep, week 2 baseline runs and golden prompt tuning, week 3 regression and edge-case testing, week 4 wrap-up and handoff. does that align?

[01:30] Markus Lee: Sounds reasonable. on infra, we prefer private deployment or dedicated pools because of PHI, but we can start hosted with de-identified data. need to confirm VPC and KMS support.

[01:45] Priya Shah: yes, security is a blocker — we need SOC2, SAML SSO, audit logs and KMS/HSM key control. also data retention policies.

[02:00] Ava Mitchell: absolutely, we'll share the SOC2 pack and the architecture options. for the quality eval — here's the proposed approach: we collect a golden set of prompts and expected outputs (gold labels) that represent typical, edge, and failure-case notes. we'll run model variants and score by a mix of automated metrics plus manual review.

[02:20] Dr. Lena Park: for scoring, what metrics do you usually use? F1 for NER, ROUGE or BERTScore for summaries? and how do you measure hallucinations?

[02:35] Diego Ramos: good question. we typically use: F1 for structured extraction; for summarization we use a composite: ROUGE-L + BERTScore + an entailment-based check to detect hallucination. additionally, we run hallucination-specific tests: prompt the model to assert facts from the note that aren't present — if it invents details, that's a fail. we add a human spot-check sample for any cases flagged by the checker.

[03:05] Ava Mitchell: to make it concrete, success criteria NovaHealth suggested earlier were: 1) Extract meds/conditions with >= 0.92 F1 on golden set, 2) Summaries with < 3% hallucination by entailment heuristics and < 10% human flagged hallucinations, 3) Format adherence (JSON schema) 99% or better, and 4) average p50 latency < 300ms and cost within target. is that still accurate?

[03:35] Dr. Lena Park: yes that's in the ballpark. we might be flexible on latency but accuracy and hallucination are non-negotiable.

[03:45] Markus Lee: on workload sizing, peak expected requests ~100 qps, average payload ~1.2k tokens, typical user flow 3 calls per session. for the POC we'll send a representative 10k-request workload to measure throughput and cost.

[04:10] Diego Ramos: excellent. we'll bootstrap with smaller samples then ramp to 10k. for benchmarks we will capture token throughput, p50/p90/p99 latencies, cost per 1k tokens, and quality metrics per golden set. we'll provide a benchmark runner that runs locally or in your env.

[04:30] Priya Shah: about data privacy, if we run in hosted mode we will only send de-identified notes. but for production we will need private deployment with VPC and customer-managed KMS. can you confirm Redwood supports HSM-backed keys?

[04:45] Ava Mitchell: yes, Redwood Private supports KMS integrations and HSM options via partners; we'll include that in the security pack. audit logs and per-request tracing are available in the console.

[04:58] Dr. Lena Park: regarding the golden prompts, can you say more about structure? we want a prompt that always returns a JSON with fields: summary, key_findings, meds_list, conditions_list, confidence_score.

[05:12] Diego Ramos: recommendation is to create a strict prompt template with example pairs — few-shot style — and include an output schema and validation step. we'll also create negative examples to test hallucination: e.g., notes that mention 'no meds' and see if model invents meds. the prompt set will include 1) typical notes, 2) edge cases (abbreviations, OCR errors), 3) adversarial examples for hallucination testing.

[05:40] Ava Mitchell: for regression tests, we maintain a suite keyed by prompt IDs. each new model version is run against the suite and we track regressions relative to the baseline model. regressions are classified by severity: minor (format changes), major (accuracy drop >3 F1 points), critical (hallucination increase >X or major data leakage).

[06:05] Dr. Lena Park: how do you handle score aggregation? per-prompt, per-patient, per-run?

[06:12] Diego Ramos: typically we compute per-example metrics then aggregate to weighted averages — we weight by clinical relevance (Lena, you'll help tag which cases are high-priority). we also produce confusion matrices for NER and per-field pass/fail for schema validation. the scoring dashboard will show baseline vs candidate and auto-flag regressions beyond thresholds.

[06:40] Markus Lee: what's the planned timeline and checkpoints?

[06:45] Ava Mitchell: proposed 4-week POC: Week 0 (kickoff) data transfer + security review; Week 1 onboarding + golden prompt creation; Week 2 baseline runs and model tuning; Week 3 regression + edge-case sweep; Week 4 final analysis and decision. milestones: mid-point checkpoint end of week 2, demo of baseline results and go/no-go.

[07:05] Dr. Lena Park: ok. do you have a suggested size for the golden set?

[07:10] Diego Ramos: for meaningful stats, aim for 800-1200 labeled examples for summarization and 1k-2k examples for NER, but we can start with 200 de-identified notes to iterate quickly and enlarge during POC.

[07:28] Priya Shah: onboarding data flow — we need an architecture diagram. also retention controls: max 30 days for POC artifacts unless otherwise agreed.

[07:38] Ava Mitchell: note taken. we'll share the architecture doc and retention policy.

[07:45] Dr. Lena Park: about hallucination measurement — you mentioned entailment checks. can you expand?

[07:50] Diego Ramos: sure. we run an NLI-style verifier: given the model's summary sentence and the source note, we run an entailment model to check if summary facts are supported. sentences with low entailment scores are flagged as potential hallucinations. we also run surface checks for invented PHIs or medications not in note — those are high severity.

[08:15] Dr. Lena Park: that makes sense. how about format checks? can we enforce strict JSON schema and fail if not matched?

[08:20] Diego Ramos: yep — output validation is baked into the runner. we provide a schema and a parser with graceful fallback logs; if the model outputs invalid JSON we treat as format failure and count towards meeting the 99% schema pass target.

[08:35] Ava Mitchell: we'll also capture token accounting and cost per 1k tokens so you can make an ROI decision.

[08:40] Markus Lee: any constraints on model variants? we want to compare 3 variants: open LLM baseline (quantized), Redwood-verified variant, and a high-accuracy candidate.

[08:50] Diego Ramos: that's standard. runner supports parallel experiments and automated comparison. we'll label baseline vs candidate and produce per-metric delta reports.

[09:02] Dr. Lena Park: what about manual review? how many human raters and what sampling strategy?

[09:08] Diego Ramos: we recommend a stratified random sample of 200 examples for human review at each checkpoint, oversampling edge-case buckets. reviewers should use a rubric: correctness, hallucination, clinical risk, format. we'll provide the rubric template.

[09:25] Priya Shah: is there a way to redact PD/PII automatically before sending to hosted env? auto-deid?

[09:30] Ava Mitchell: Redwood has integrations for de-id pipelines; we can run an extra de-identification pass or you can supply de-identified data. we'll document options.

[09:40] Markus Lee: let's confirm the acceptance criteria again so everyone is aligned.

[09:45] Ava Mitchell: acceptance criteria (recap): 1) NER meds/conditions F1 >= 0.92 on golden set; 2) summary hallucination rate <= 3% by entailment checks and <= 10% human-flagged; 3) JSON schema pass rate >= 99%; 4) Throughput support for 100 qps with p99 latency target of X (we'll be flexible), and cost within the agreed budget. if any critical regressions occur we won't proceed to production until fixed.

[10:15] Dr. Lena Park: sounds good. what's the plan for handoff if POC succeeds?

[10:20] Ava Mitchell: handoff doc with recommended deployment mode (Dedicated vs Private), runbook, and model/version pinning. also a rollout plan with canaries and fallback to a safer model if regressions are detected.

[10:33] Diego Ramos: we'll also provide the baseline artifacts and evaluation harness as a reproducible repo you can run internally.

[10:40] Priya Shah: please include SAML SSO setup steps and required IP allowlists.

[10:45] Ava Mitchell: will do.

[10:48] Markus Lee: ok next steps?

[10:50] Ava Mitchell: action items recap: Ava to send security docs + pricing by Friday; Diego to share initial golden prompt examples and benchmark runner; NovaHealth to send 200 de-identified sample notes and identify top 50 high-priority cases. we'll schedule the baseline run for week 2 and checkpoint at the end of week 2.

[11:10] Dr. Lena Park: thanks, appreciate it.

[11:12] Ava Mitchell: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the doc links.

End of transcript.
